title: Adaptive intake lattice for model additions, staged version anchoring, and deprecation cadence
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: High-volume enterprise requests for new model variants and version requests are creating ad-hoc pinning, surprise regressions, and manual deprecation negotiation. Current intake is reactive and lacks a consistent way to balance customer SLAs, evaluation risk, and infrastructure cost. This causes delays for customers and operational burden for SRE/Runtime teams.

Goal: Define and implement an adaptive intake lattice that scores incoming model/addition requests across business and technical signals, supports staged version anchoring (an alternative to one-off permanent pins), and codifies a deprecation cadence tied to usage and regression telemetry. The system should provide clear gates for enterprise customers, visibility to SEs, and automated guardrails for runtime and eval teams.

Scope: Product-facing triage logic, intake form updates, new catalog metadata fields, evaluation gating criteria, routing/shadowing rules, and deprecation scheduling workflow. Implementation will include a console surface for reviewers, a triage scorer service (lightweight), and acceptance/rollback playbooks for flagged regressions. This ticket is non-bug / PM feature work and will coordinate closely with ENG, Design, Security, and Solutions Engineering.
Out-of-scope: Full runtime autoscaling changes, billing model overhaul, and on-prem installation specifics (these will be follow-ups with Dedicated/Private teams if needed).
acceptance_criteria: Intake form updated with required fields: customer-tier, data-residency, estimated qps, expected token mix, rationale for variant, and compatibility constraints.
Triage lattice implemented as a scoring doc + prototype service that produces a ranked outcome (Fast-Path, Staged-Anchoring, Shadow-Probe, Manual Review).
Console review UI wireframes and a minimal interactive prototype available for internal SEs and PMs.
Staged version anchoring workflow documented: initial anchor window, decay schedule, and automatic re-eval triggers based on eval regressions or adoption signals.
Eval gating rules codified: threshold for acceptable regression, required set of customer-like prompts, and automated smoke tests run on onboarding PRs.
Shadow exposure mechanism implemented so new variants can be routed to <= X% of traffic with full telemetry and automatic cutoff on regression or SLA violation.
Runbook for deprecations that defines notice windows by customer tier, automated notification templates, and an archival procedure for metrics/evals.
Cross-functional sign-off from Eng (runtime), Security, Design, and Solutions Engineering documented as approvals in comments.
Pilot executed with 2 enterprise customers and learnings collected in a short retro document.
No security review outstanding at release: security_review_required set to true and security sign-off attached.

decisions: Use a multi-dimensional score (business_impact, regression_risk, infra_cost, data_sensitivity, customer_priority) instead of a single binary lane — provides finer granularity for staged exposure.
Introduce 'staged version anchoring' (timeboxed anchors) instead of permanent pins by default. Permanent anchors require explicit sponsor and contract exception.
Shadow-probe exposure cap default set to 2% of traffic for the first 14 days, with automatic rollback if any critical metric drops >5% relative to baseline.
Require a canonical eval set that mirrors customer prompts for any enterprise onboarding; lightweight 'compatibility quickchecks' will be run in CI.
Console will show recommended action + rationale (score breakdown) to avoid opaque reviewer decisions.
Security review required prior to granting Fast-Path/Anchored status for variants that process customer PII or fall under data-residency constraints.
Deprecation cadence: candidates with <1% catalog usage for 90 days move to 'sunset-proposed' and notified; exceptions for enterprise-anchored variants.
Adopt an audit log schema for intake decisions to support future ML audits and compliance requests.
risks: Overly complex lattice could slow triage — mitigate by limiting to top 5 signals and defaulting non-specified fields to conservative values.
Shadow routing might increase operational noise in telemetry dashboards — add auto-aggregation and a separate 'probe' dashboard.
Customers may treat staged anchors as permanent if not communicated clearly — require templated notifications and clear UI language.
False negatives in eval gating (missed regressions) — mandate both unit-level smoke tests and a small set of real-customer shadow prompts where feasible.
Security/compliance edge cases for on-prem/private variants — escalate to Private team and treat as manual review until resolved.
notes: Trade-offs considered: fast acceptance vs risk control. We prioritize default conservative actions for unknowns, with a clear path to accelerate (fast-path) when warranted.
Operational cost: shadow probes will add metric cardinality; plan to cap number of concurrent probes and reuse probe buckets across similar requests.
Design asks: we need a clear, human-readable score explainer and inline links to required artifacts (eval results, PRs, customer agreement).
Possible follow-ups: integration with billing to surface infra cost impact to customers and an SLA escrow for anchored variants.
